title: Mass of the Alice-bit deviation event on the zero–zero slice
statement:
Fix a positive integer $n$ and a deterministic communication protocol $p$ for the length-$n$ set-disjointness problem, and let $\gamma > 0$. Work under the hard distribution on samples $\omega$, each of which determines a special coordinate $T$, Alice's and Bob's input sets $X$ and $Y$ (with special bits $x_T$ and $y_T$), and the transcript $M$ produced by $p$ on input $(X,Y)$. For a value $z$ of the variable $Z = (M, T, X_{<T}, Y_{>T})$, let $\delta_X(z)$ be the total variation distance between the conditional law of $x_T$ given $\{Z = z\}$ and the uniform distribution on one bit. Suppose that, under the hard distribution conditioned on the disjointness event $X \cap Y = \varnothing$,
\[ I\big(x_T ; M \mid T,\, X_{<T},\, Y_{\ge T}\big) \;+\; I\big(y_T ; M \mid T,\, X_{\le T},\, Y_{>T}\big) \;\le\; \frac{2\gamma^4}{3}. \]
Then the hard distribution assigns mass at most $\gamma/2$ to the set of samples for which both special bits vanish, $x_T = y_T = 0$, and $\delta_X(Z) > \gamma$.
hypotheses_covered: a deterministic protocol $p$ for length-$n$ disjointness
conditional-mutual-information bound $I(x_T;M\mid T,X_{<T},Y_{\ge T}) + I(y_T;M\mid T,X_{\le T},Y_{>T}) \le 2\gamma^4/3$ under the disjointness-conditioned hard distribution
replaced: Alice marginal estimate: under the $(X_{T},Y_{T})=(0,0)$ slice, the set of $Z$ fibers whose Alice special-bit marginal is farther than $γ$ from uniform has mass at most $γ / 2$.
